justification: KEY COLLISION between two distinct operations that happen to share the literal path+method 'GET /usage' in their respective documents. openapi.yaml documents the real, tenant-scoped /v1 billing endpoint (tag Billing, operationId getUsage, usage:read scope) added independently of this exemption. The gateway ALSO serves a gateway-native, operator-only telemetry endpoint at the bare host root (tag internal, WAVE service bearer, no /v1 prefix) that this repo cannot document at this same key without overwriting the real customer endpoint's declaration — the two must live at the same path string in the published document because the operator route was never given a distinguishing per-operation servers override (unlike its siblings /leaderboard and /platform, which do carry one). This entry exempts ONLY the operator shape (matched by its 'internal' tag, which never appears on the real customer operation); it lapses the moment the published operation at this key stops being tagged internal, forcing a fresh look rather than silently re-exempting whatever answers here.

The gateway still serves the auto-generated skills-index open placeholder shape (not x-schema-status: draft — that means 'not observed live' here) for this operation (lowercase tag, no operationId, a summary that says 'draft — see api-spec for the full shape' and literally defers to this repo). openapi.yaml has since promoted this to a fully hand-documented /v1 operation (real params, description, Streams tag, operationId listStreams) ahead of the gateway shipping the matching handler. Exempt only while the published operation still has no operationId — the moment the gateway ships the real handler and starts publishing one, this predicate fails and the exemption lapses so the two shapes get compared for real.

Same shape and same reasoning as GET /streams: the published operation is still the auto-generated open placeholder shape (not x-schema-status: draft — that means 'not observed live' here) (no operationId), while openapi.yaml documents the real, hand-specified /v1 operation (operationId createStream) ahead of the gateway shipping it. Lapses the moment the published operation gains an operationId.

The service's own generated 400 response for this operation is a single, coarser schema ($ref Error) with a shorter description; openapi.yaml documents a oneOf of the WAVE error envelope AND the RFC 8628 §3.5 device-flow error passthrough (authorization_pending / slow_down / expired_token / access_denied / invalid_grant) verbatim, which is the actual, more detailed behavior of this endpoint. This is the service's own OpenAPI reflection being less precise than this repo's hand-written documentation, not a real behavioral difference this repo needs to walk back. Keyed on the exact current published 400 description so a real future change to the service's generated shape still surfaces as drift rather than being silently re-exempted.

expect.responses.200.description: Speech generated.
